pointers.sibling: JSON schema of the lease calls and records
N-06 Service units, clock and health
pointers.principle: Rule 2 (no cog: expiry by the clock, never by opinion) and rule 3 (three attempts then report)
The collision answer every node gives: leases with fencing tokens, compare-and-swap, idempotent steps, conflicts that report
pointers.shared: The lease states, transitions, guards and who calls each

shared-needs.rule: Each need names the shared volume and anchor that holds the rule; check.sh resolves it. A number written in a shared contract is cited, never restated here.
shared-needs.need: Rows for lease.recovered 100; lease.granted 201; lease.released 204; lease.stale 412; lease.refused 423 (held, hold) and 429 (cap); lease.expired 500; lease.failed 500. lease.renewed, lease.started and lease.revoked are not records (shared/contracts.xml#statements).

leases(key PRIMARY KEY, class, ticket, phase, attempt, state, token INTEGER, generation, holder NOT NULL, run_id, granted_at, expires_at, heartbeat_at, progress_at, ended_at, end_reason, version), the row of shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_row; the token counter is entity counter:lease_token.
The fencing token only grows; fencing is by lease key and token (shared/contracts.xml#fencing).
Two seats can never both act on one ticket phase; a silent seat loses its lease by time.
Liveness is a timestamp and the process table, never a pane read or a model opinion (V08, K04).
The launcher (N-15), not the model, renews; every node reads the same timing keys.

lease.ttl_seconds, lease.heartbeat_seconds, start.grace_seconds, lease.leader_ttl_seconds, lease.keep_days, caps.max_seats (defaults in shared/contracts.xml#timing); jobs.in_flight and lease.caps are dropped. A missing key is exit 3 naming the key; exit 4 is reserved for a duplicate instance (nodes/N-06/spec.xml#mechanism).
A lease past expires_at: swept to expired, lease.expired 500; N-12 stops the run, N-11 decides attempt n+1.

purpose.is: N-02 owns the leases table and its state machine (shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine): one row per lease key, one holder that is never empty, one integer fencing token that only grows, one expiry, a generation that grows only on a grant, and a state of reserved, running, released, expired or revoked.

It is the collision answer of the whole factory: two runs can never both act on one ticket phase, a run that went silent loses its lease by time, and a write under a lease that is not current is refused by N-01's fence.
purpose.is-not: It does not decide to dispatch (N-07 calls GrantDispatch), does not kill a run (shared/contracts.xml#kill-authority), does not retry (N-11), and never asks a model whether a holder is alive (SPEC-16 l-llm, K04).
purpose.decisions: D01, D17 (C49), D02 (C36), T06 (lease with heartbeat, generation counter, compare-and-swap, never stolen while liveness is unknown); review disposition F05.

record.field: What a seat lease will be keyed on: ticket:phase:attempt (shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/seat_lease_key). N-07 reads ready tickets with no reserved or running lease for (ticket, phase) and grants inside its GrantDispatch Commit; N-02 never grants on its own.

also.from: N-15 launcher through Lease.Renew; a system holder in-process
N-15 on seat.result; a system holder at the end of its job
a system holder in-process (N-07 leader, N-09 merge.lock, N-27 watchers, N-05 backup, N-45 cleanup)

record.field: A seat key (class seat) or a system key (class work or maintenance), shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_key.
reserved for a seat grant; running for a system acquire.
The dispatch id for a seat lease; the node and job for a system lease; never empty.
The next value of counter:lease_token, an integer; every later token for any key is larger.
Grants of this key so far; it grows only on a grant (GrantDispatch, a free regrant, an Acquire), never on renew, sweep or revoke.
granted_at plus start.grace_seconds for a reserved seat lease; plus the class ttl for a running system lease.

output.record: reserved or running to released by the holder's token.
The sweep found the lease past expires_at; end_reason start-grace for a reserved lease (a free regrant, no attempt charged, shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner) or expired for a running one.

A grant or acquire refused: held (another holder is reserved or running) or hold (flag:hold under a seat grant or a work-class acquire); 429 for cap (caps.max_seats). The refused Commit wrote nothing; N-02 appends this record in a separate Commit only when the reason for a key changes, never every tick. A GrantDispatch refused for a precondition (a spent key, a ticket version) is a 412 reply and no lease record.
A Start, Renew or Release whose token, generation or state is not current; logged, nothing changed.
output.rule: Start, Renew and Revoke append no lease record (shared/contracts.xml#statements): Start moves the run entity run:<run_id> in the same Commit, Renew is entity-only (shared/contracts.xml#entity-only), and N-12 appends its stall record in the Revoke Commit. lease.granted is appended by leases.grant inside N-07's GrantDispatch: node N-02 (the statement's owner), by N-07 (the caller N-01 derived).

api.service: Start(key, token, run_id), Renew(key, token, generation, progress_at), Release(key, token, result). Callers: the launcher (coq-launch, shared/authority.xml#role-derivation) for its own run's lease only; run_id equals the dispatch id. Each call is one Commit on N-01 under the lease reference with the operation keys of shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys (N-15/run.start/<run_id>/r1, N-15/lease.renew/<run_id>@<beat>/r1). Errors map as nodes/N-01/spec.xml#api.

statements.rule: N-02 registers the leases.* statements of shared/contracts.xml#statements and implements the rows of shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine exactly; the guards, effects and refusal codes are those rows, not restated here. What this node adds is how each guard reads the table.
statements.statement: Reads the row for the key (absent, or released or expired with a free regrant recorded by N-11), counts seat rows reserved or running against caps.max_seats, reads flag:hold, and inserts or rewrites the row with the next counter:lease_token in the same transaction.
Same reads for a work or maintenance key; a work key also reads flag:hold; a re-acquire by the same holder of a running row is a replay of its operation key, not a second grant.
One UPDATE ... WHERE key AND token AND state = reserved AND expires_at > now; zero rows is 412.

One UPDATE ... WHERE key AND token AND generation AND state IN (reserved, running) AND expires_at > now; zero rows is 412 and lease.stale. The launcher sends the generation it was granted so a mismatch is caught even if a token were ever reused.
One UPDATE ... WHERE key AND token AND state IN (reserved, running) AND expires_at > now; zero rows is 412 and lease.stale.
One UPDATE per key WHERE state IN (reserved, running) AND expires_at <= now, operation key N-02/lease.sweep/<key>@<token>/r1.
One UPDATE ... WHERE key AND version = judged version AND state IN (reserved, running); zero rows is 409 version (a fresh heartbeat wins) and N-12 re-judges.
statements.rule: No statement clears the holder; no statement moves the generation except grant and acquire.

mechanism.component: Go package scheduler/internal/lease: the seven statements above, registered with N-01 at start (shared/contracts.xml#statements), plus Current(key, token) for N-01's fence. Pure arithmetic for expiry; the clock is core.Clock.

leases in coq.db, owned here, one row per key, shaped as shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_row; token INTEGER; holder NOT NULL. The token counter is entity counter:lease_token, bumped by compare-and-swap in the same transaction as the grant.

seat: a ticket phase, granted only by GrantDispatch. work: merge.lock, publish:drive, cutover:run; refused under hold. maintenance: node:N-07:leader, watcher/*, backup:*, cleanup:*, workspace:*, seat:*, tier:*, drain:*; allowed under hold, because the leader, the watchers, backups and cleanup must keep running while the line is held.
caps.max_seats counts seat-class leases in reserved or running. One cap, data in config; jobs.in_flight and lease.caps are dropped.
mechanism.fence: Current(key, token) for N-01's step 3: true when the row exists, its state is reserved or running, its token equals the presented token and now is before expires_at. A key names the ticket, the phase and the attempt, so the worker and the reviewer of one attempt never share a fence, and a system key fences a system job that has no ticket.
mechanism.terminal: For the terminal report of shared/contracts.xml#terminal-report, N-02 answers whether a token is the most recent token of a revoked or expired row; N-01 admits that one report per run_id with fenced true.
mechanism.desired: A lease that ended (released, expired, revoked) is never claimable by its own key again except by a free regrant; N-07's desired set is tickets ready, not_before passed, with no reserved or running lease for (ticket, phase), so an ended lease cannot loop back into dispatch. A new attempt is a new key (N-11 owns n+1).
mechanism.timing: lease.ttl_seconds, lease.heartbeat_seconds, start.grace_seconds and the leader ttl are the values of shared/contracts.xml#timing; the launcher renews every heartbeat, far inside the ttl, so a service restart of a few minutes never expires a live run; N-12's dead-launcher bound is three missed heartbeats.
mechanism.liveness: A lease is never stolen while liveness is unknown: it ends only by its token (release), by the clock (sweep) or by N-12's revoke at a judged version. No probe, no screen read, no model opinion (V08, K04).

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. Grants run inside N-07's tick; Sweep runs on every stall tick from N-06; Start, Renew and Release are calls the launcher makes as code around the one-shot run.
start.step: At service start, after the store opens: Recover sweeps every reserved or running row past expires_at; every unexpired row is left alone (a seat in its own systemd unit survives a service restart, nodes/N-06/spec.xml#mechanism, and keeps its lease and token).
Config is loaded; a missing key is exit 3 naming the key.
lease.recovered 100 is appended once with the counts swept and kept.

wait.name: grant-commit
wait.fallback: 503 from the store; N-07 treats the ticket as not dispatched this tick and tries next tick with the same operation key

wait.name: start-grace
wait.on: the launcher calling Start on a reserved lease
wait.fallback: the sweep expires it with end_reason start-grace; no attempt is charged; the ticket is ready again for N-07

wait.name: heartbeat
wait.on: the holder renewing a running lease
wait.fallback: the sweep expires it; lease.expired 500; N-12 stops the run per shared/contracts.xml#kill-authority, N-11 decides attempt n+1

wait.name: sweep
wait.timeout: stall.tick_seconds; a sweep older than 3 ticks is reported by N-06 health as tick.missed
wait.fallback: the next tick sweeps; a missed sweep delays expiry, never loses it

wait.name: cap
wait.timeout: none held here: a 429 returns at once
wait.fallback: N-07 re-evaluates every tick; nothing blocks on a cap

wait.name: hold
wait.timeout: none held here: a 423 hold returns at once
wait.fallback: N-07 re-evaluates every tick; maintenance leases keep running; the owner clears the hold through N-42 and N-29

retries.rule: Who retries is decided in shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner; N-02 never re-grants on its own.
retries.step: A 503 is retried by N-07 next tick with the same operation key, so a retry replays or commits once; a 409 on counter:lease_token inside the transaction cannot happen (the single writer serializes it). After 3 failed ticks on one key N-07 appends lease.failed 500; three on one key in ten minutes is owner-acts through N-28.
The launcher retries a 503 within the heartbeat; a 412 is final: the run is not current and the launcher stops it and writes its terminal report.
A release that cannot commit is left to the sweep; lease.expired names the result id that tried to release, so the record is evidence, not a lost release.
A sweep transaction failing is retried next tick; one transaction per key, so one bad row cannot stop the others.

many-agents.reading: The launcher reads its own run's lease by key; the token travels only in the dispatch and the launcher's environment, never to the seat (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation).
many-agents.working: Sixteen seats hold sixteen seat leases (caps.max_seats); system holders hold their own keys; the store serializes every statement.
many-agents.collision: Two N-07 ticks grant one key: the GrantDispatch operation key (N-07/dispatch/<lease_key>@<token>) and the guard admit one; the other is 423 held and does not dispatch.
The sweep expired a lease, then the old launcher renews or releases: state is expired, the guard fails, 412 lease_not_current, lease.stale; the lease is not revived (NF-A2 closed).
N-12 revoked attempt 1 and N-11 cut attempt 2 on a new key: attempt 1's writes are 412; its one terminal seat.result is admitted with fenced true and N-11 treats it as an echo, not a new failure.
Release and Sweep race on an expiring lease: both are statements on one row behind the single writer; the first wins; the loser's guard fails and is logged.
N-12 judged version v and revokes while the launcher renews to v+1: the revoke's version guard fails, N-12 re-reads and re-judges on the fresh heartbeat.
The owner holds the line while N-07 restarts: node:N-07:leader is maintenance class and is acquired under hold, so the line stays held by one leader, not by none.
many-agents.test: Two grantors per key over 100 keys, 1000 rounds, a fake clock stepping past start grace and ttl, revokes at random versions: one grant per generation, tokens strictly increasing across all keys, no write accepted under a token that is not current, every renew after expiry refused.

emits.acts: N-07 (it wrote the dispatch in the same Commit), N-12
nobody; evidence that a fenced call was refused
N-07 waits a tick; N-40 shows the cap pressure
N-12 stops the run, N-11 decides attempt n+1 (no charge on start-grace)
N-07 next tick; three in ten minutes on one key is a card through N-28

status-codes.rule: Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes with the same meaning and actor.

path.cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-leases.sh: --dry-run lists released, expired or revoked rows older than lease.keep_days; --apply deletes them; never a reserved or running row

state-paths.rule: No other path. A lease is a row, never a file; herdr/config/leases.json and the treehouse slot lease are retired by N-14 and N-49.

in.note: calls, not drawn as DAG edges

re-entry.note: gate.verdict green re-enters as a reviewer-phase grant on the same ticket
attempt n+1 re-enters as a new key

item.check: GrantDispatch on a free key returns state reserved, a token larger than every earlier token, generation plus one and a non-empty holder, in the same Commit as the dispatch and the ticket transition.
A reserved lease not started within start.grace_seconds is swept with end_reason start-grace, and N-11 charges no attempt.
item.proof: Go test with the fake clock (not-run).

item.check: Renew and Release after expiry or revoke return 412 and change nothing; Renew with a wrong generation returns 412.
Renew appends no record; ten renews leave ten heartbeat entity versions and zero records.
Under flag:hold, GrantDispatch and a work-class Acquire are 423; node:N-07:leader and a watcher lease are acquired.
Over caps.max_seats a grant is 429 and the count is exact under concurrency.
item.proof: Go test with 32 goroutines on cap 16 (not-run).

item.check: Every system key of shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/system_lease_key can be acquired; generation moves only on grant and acquire.
Recover at start keeps unexpired leases and sweeps expired ones.
A missing config key exits 3 naming it.
item.proof: `scheduler check` output with the key removed (not-run).

item.check: cleanup-leases.sh dry-run lists and never deletes a reserved or running row.

actor.name: system holders in-process (N-05, N-07, N-09, N-27, N-45)
actor.may: leases.acquire, renew, release on their own keys

actor.name: N-15 launcher (coq-launch)
actor.may: Lease.Start, Renew, Release for the lease of the run it launched

actor.name: seat (the model inside the run)
actor.may: nothing: no token, no socket, no lease call

actor.name: owner
actor.may: `scheduler ctl lease release KEY --break-glass` once, recorded as break.glass; never automated

gauge.name: lease.cap_pressure
gauge.note: seat leases reserved or running divided by caps.max_seats

counter.name: lease.stale_total
counter.alarm: any: a fenced call was attempted

monitoring.surface: Machine screen (N-39) shows a node's lease (state, holder, token, expires_at); Alerts (N-41) shows lease.expired; Stats (N-40) shows cap pressure.

runbook.task: `scheduler ctl lease get WO-ID` prints every phase and attempt row with state, holder, token, generation, expiry.
Do nothing by hand: N-12 judges the stall and revokes, or the sweep expires it; the Alerts screen shows it. A hand release is break glass only.
Edit scheduler/config/scheduler.json through a ticket; `scheduler ctl reload` applies it; a running lease keeps its old expiry until its next renew.

item.what: four lease kinds (slot, tier, ticket, seat) with ttls declared but enforced by a monitor
item.reason: declared and not enforced (L02 section 6, finding 7); one table with three classes, enforced by the sweep

item.what: lease_ttl_seconds 7200 with renew_grace_seconds 300 enforced only when sweep runs
item.reason: three queue implementations with lease fields nobody swept (K05, S03 F1); the sweep is a tick here

item.what: the seats domain with caps, holding and the shared merger seat
item.reason: caps are kept as data; the merger seat is killed (D11 C39: code merges)

item.what: a separate renewal token beside the fencing token
item.reason: one number that only grows answers both

item.what: a lease with no state, cleared by emptying the holder (book 1.0)
item.reason: an ended lease looked free and looped back into dispatch, and Release succeeded after the sweep (NF-A2, NF2); the state column and a holder that is never empty replace it
it refused the leader and the watchers, the monitoring that must never stop; hold gates only seat grants and work-class acquires

item.what: a monitor that releases an expired slot lease after reading a pane
item.reason: an LLM opinion is not a probe (V08); expiry is the clock
